23           Plaintiff, Quanergy Solutions, Inc. f/k/a Rolisi, LLC (“Plaintiff” or “Quanergy”), by and
24 through its undersigned counsel, Fox Rothschild LLP, and pursuant to Rule 8 of the Federal Rules

25 of Civil Procedure asserts the following claims against Defendant Prime Communications, Inc.

26 d/b/a Prime Secured (“Defendant” or “Prime Secured”) and in support thereof alleges as follows:

27                                                  PARTIES
28           1.        Quanergy is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business in San

                                                      -1-                                       COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
             Case 5:24-cv-08671           Document 1         Filed 12/03/24   Page 2 of 12


 1 Jose, California.

 2              2.      Prime Secured is a Nebraska corporation with its principal place of business in

 3 Elkhorn, Nebraska.

 4                                          JURISDICTION AND VENUE

 5              3.      This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 28 U.S.C.
 6 Section 1332 based on complete diversity of citizenship inasmuch as Quanergy is deemed a citizen

 7 of California (the state where the principal place of business is located) and Delaware (the state of

 8 incorporation) and Prime Secured is a citizen of Nebraska.

 9              4.      The amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.
10              5.      This Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant Prime Secured because said
11 defendant expressly consented to personal jurisdiction in California as set forth more fully below.

12              6.      Furthermore, this Court has personal jurisdiction over Defendant Prime Secured be-
13 cause said defendant directed business activities toward and conducted business with parties

14 within the State of California and the claims asserted herein arise from said activities.

15              7.      Venue is proper in this Court under 28 U.S.C. Section 1391(b) because a substan-
16 tial part of the events and injury occurred in the Northern District of California and, in the alterna-

17 tive, under Section 1391(b)(3). Further, venue is proper in this Court under the forum selection

18 clause in the Agreement. See Ex. A § 12.8.

19                                          DIVISIONAL ASSIGNMENT
20              8.      Assignment to the San Jose Division of this District is proper pursuant to Northern
21 District of California Civil Local Rule 3-2(c) because a substantial part of the events that gave rise

22 to Plaintiff’s claims occurred in the County of Santa Clara.

23                                               OPERATIVE FACTS
24              A. Quanergy-Prime Secured Systems Integrator Direct Purchase Agreement
25              9.      At all times relevant hereto, non-party Quanergy Systems, Inc. (“Quanergy
26 OldCo”) was a manufacturer of LiDAR 1 sensors and related proprietary products, technology, ma-

27 terials and software (“Products”).

28
     1
         The term “LiDAR” stands for Light Detection and Ranging.

                                                            -2-                                   COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671        Document 1       Filed 12/03/24      Page 3 of 12


 1           10.     At all times relevant hereto, Prime Secured engaged was a provider of, inter alia,

 2 enterprise physical security services, commercial physical security services and managed IT ser-

 3 vices.

 4           11.     On or about June 30, 2021, Quanergy OldCo and Prime Secured entered into that

 5 certain Systems Integrator Direct Purchase Agreement (the “Agreement”), a true and correct copy

 6 of which is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

 7           12.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Quanergy OldCo appointed Prime Secured as its non-

 8 exclusive Systems Integrator and reseller of Products in North America (the “Territory”) for a

 9 term of three (3) years commencing on June 30, 2021, and ending on June 30, 2024 (the “Term”).

10           13.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Prime Secured agreed to purchase not less than 500

11 units of Products and other services during the Term.

12           14.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Prime Secured agreed to use its best efforts to market,

13 promote, sell and support the Products throughout the Territory.

14           15.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Prime Secured agreed to maintain technological sys-

15 tems and capabilities needed to effectively market the Products to end users.

16           16.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Prime Secured agreed to employ sufficient personnel

17 with knowledge and training necessary to effectively sell the Products.

18           17.     Pursuant to the Agreement, Prime Secured agreed to promptly pay for Products ac-

19 tually ordered.

20           B. Purchase Order PO-67482

21           18.     The Agreement, at Section 3.1, provided that “SI shall purchase Quanergy Products

22 by issuing a Purchase Order.”

23           19.     On June 30, 2022, Prime Secured issued and delivered purchase order No. PO-

24 67482 (the “Purchase Order”) to Quanergy OldCo. A true and correct copy of the Purchase Order

25 is attached hereto as Exhibit B.

26           20.     Pursuant to the Purchase Order, Prime Secured ordered 100 M8-1 POE sensors at a

27 price of $288,800, 400 MQ-8 POE-Plus sensors at a price of $1,532,000, and 500 perpetual soft-

28 ware licenses for the both sensors at a price of $792,000 for a total order of $2,612,800.


                                                     -3-                                        COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671         Document 1       Filed 12/03/24    Page 4 of 12


 1           21.    By sales order No. 105036 dated June 30, 2022 (“Sales Order”), Quanergy OldCo

 2 confirmed the Purchase Order and agreed to ship the Products by June 30, 2024. A true and cor-

 3 rect copy of the Sales Order is attached hereto as Exhibit C.

 4           22.    The shipment date was consistent with the Agreement inasmuch as this was a back-

 5 log Purchase Order intended to ensure a steady supply of Products and avoid supply chain inter-

 6 ruptions.

 7           C. Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Filing and §363 Sale

 8           23.    On December 12, 2022 (“Petition Date”), Quanergy OldCo filed a voluntary peti-

 9 tion for relief under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code (the “Bankruptcy Code”) in

10 the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware (the “Bankruptcy Court”) under

11 Docket No. 22-11305-CTG (“the Bankruptcy Case”).

12           24.    On December 13, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court issued an order (the “Bidding Proce-

13 dures Order”) approving bidding procedures in connection with the sale of Quanergy OldCo’s as-

14 sets in accordance with, inter alia, Section 363 of the Bankruptcy Code (the “Section 363 Sale”).

15           25.    On January 30, 2023, Plaintiff (then known as Rolisi, LLC) was determined to be

16 the successful bidder (the “Successful Bidder”) for the assets sold pursuant to the Section 363

17 Sale.

18           26.    On or about February 1, 2023, and subject to Bankruptcy Court approval, Plaintiff

19 entered into that certain Asset Purchase Agreement with Quanergy OldCo for the purchase of sub-

20 stantially all of the seller’s tangible and intangible assets.

21           27.    Pursuant to an order dated February 2, 2023 (the “§363 Sale Order”), the Bank-

22 ruptcy Court approved the sale of substantially all of the tangible and intangible assets of Quan-

23 ergy OldCo to Plaintiff.

24           28.    On February 3, 2023, Plaintiff closed on the sale and, thus, acquired substantially

25 of Quanergy OldCo’s tangible and intangible assets.

26           29.    Among other things, Plaintiff acquired all rights to the name “Quanergy”.

27           30.    On or about March 13, 2023, Plaintiff converted from a Florida limited liability

28 company formerly known as Rolisi, LLC to a Delaware corporation known as Quanergy


                                                      -4-                                     COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671        Document 1        Filed 12/03/24      Page 5 of 12


 1 Solutions, Inc.

 2           31.     Pursuant to, inter alia, applicable bankruptcy law, upon the filing of the voluntary

 3 petition under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code, including 11 U.S.C. § 365(d)(d), all executory

 4 contracts in effect as of the Petition Date, including the Agreement, remained in force until and

 5 unless rejected by the debtor-in-possession Quanergy OldCo upon approval of the Bankruptcy

 6 Court.

 7           32.     In connection with the Bankruptcy Case and pursuant to Order of the Bankruptcy

 8 Court, Quanergy OldCo assumed and assigned the Agreement, an unexpired executory contract, to

 9 Plaintiff.

10           D. Defendant’s Breach

11           33.     From the Petition Date through February 3, 2023, the sale date, Quanergy OldCo

12 operated as a debtor-in-possession in accordance with Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code.

13           34.     From the Petition Date through February 3, 2023, the sale date, Quanergy OldCo

14 processed and fulfilled customer orders.

15           35.     From and after February 3, 2023, Prime Secured promised to promote Plaintiff’s

16 Products pursuant to the Agreement.

17           36.     For example, and without limitation, in connection with the International Security

18 Conference and Exposition (“ISC West”) held in Las Vegas, Nevada between March 31, 2023 and

19 April 4, 2023, Prime Secured advised that it had dedicated time to introduce Plaintiff’s technology

20 to prospective customers.

21           37.     Furthermore, in connection with the Global Security Exchange conference (“GSX”)

22 held between September 11, 2023 and September 13, 2023 in Dallas Texas, Prime Secured ad-

23 vised that Plaintiff could “count on us coming to see you and bringing some clients as well.”

24           38.     Furthermore, on November 8, 2023, Prime Secured proposed a call to share Prod-

25 uct information with prospective customers and “discuss the next steps in the sales plan”.

26           39.     On and after November 8, 2023, while Prime Secured expressed, on the surface,

27 some interest and/or willingness to make prospective customer introductions, no meaningful effort

28 was invested into the marketing or promotion of Plaintiff’s technology and Products as required


                                                     -5-                                        COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671        Document 1       Filed 12/03/24      Page 6 of 12


 1 by the Agreement.

 2           40.    Furthermore, as the June 30, 2024 deadline drew close, Steven Kanne (“Kanne”).

 3 Prime Secured’s Chief Operating Officer advised on June 19, 2024 that Prime Secured was only

 4 willing to “sell product that has not been manufactured”, i.e. new products, not Products that were

 5 ordered pursuant to the Purchase Order and Agreement.

 6           41.    The intent and effect of the June 19, 2024 was to advise that Prime Secured would

 7 not honor the obligations under the Purchase Order and Agreement.

 8           42.    At all times relevant hereto, Prime Secured conveyed its refusal to honor the Agree-

 9 ment, accept Products that were ordered, schedule and/or arrange for delivery, pay for the Prod-

10 ucts and/or discuss ongoing business relationship established under the Agreement.

11           43.    The Agreement, at Section 7.2, sets forth procedures for termination.

12           44.    Prime Secure never terminated the Agreement.

13           45.    The Agreement remains in effect.

14           46.    Any attempted cancellation or termination of a contractual obligation due to a

15 bankruptcy filing was prohibited under applicable bankruptcy law, including under 11 U.S.C. §

16 365(e)(1), was without legal effect.

17           47.    By reason of the aforesaid, Plaintiff suffered damages including, without limitation,

18 lost profits, lost business opportunities, and other damages to be established at trial.

19                                     FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION

20                                     (Breach of Written Contract)

21           48.    Plaintiff re-alleges the allegations set forth in paragraphs 1 through 47 above and

22 incorporates each allegation herein by reference.

23                                         Breach by Repudiation

24           49.    Pursuant to the Agreement and via the Purchase Order, Prime Secured ordered

25 Products and licenses at a price of $2,612,800.

26           50.    Pursuant to Section 3.3 of the Agreement, all sales are final.

27           51.    Prime Secured willfully refused to proceed with the Purchase Order and breached

28 its other obligations under the Agreement as set forth more fully herein.


                                                     -6-                                       COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671       Document 1        Filed 12/03/24     Page 7 of 12


 1           52.    Prime Secured breached the Agreement by refusing to adhere to its obligations un-

 2 der the Purchase Order and Agreement.

 3                                    Breach by Failure to Promote

 4           53.    The Agreement between Prime Secured and Quanergy specified that Prime Secured

 5 would use its best efforts to market, promote, sell and support the products throughout the Terri-

 6 tory. See Ex. A.

 7           54.    Since at least February 3, 2024, Prime Secured failed to market, promote, sell or

 8 support Quanergy’s products throughout the Territory and, thus, failed to use its best efforts to

 9 market, promote, sell and support the products.

10           55.    Sporadic promises to introduce prospective customers to Plaintiff at trade shows

11 falls far short of what is required under the Agreement.

12           56.    Prime Secured breached the Agreement by failing to use its best efforts to market,

13 promote, sell and support the products throughout the Territory.

14           57.    Pursuant to Section 3.6 of the Agreement, Prime Secured is liable for interest on

15 any delinquent amounts owed to Quanergy at the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month or (b) the maximum

16 rate permitted under California law.

17           58.    Section 3.6 of the Agreement provides that Prime Secured shall be responsible for

18 reasonable attorneys’ fees and other costs incurred by Quanergy in connection with litigation to

19 enforce the Agreement if Quanergy prevails.

20           59.    As a direct and proximate result of the material breach of the Agreement by Prime

21 Secured, Quanergy has sustained general, special and incidental damages in an amount not less

22 than $2,612,800 plus interest at the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month or (b) the maximum rate permit-

23 ted under California law, and Quanergy’s reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs.

24           60.    Furthermore, as a direct and proximate result of Prime Secured’s breaches, Quan-

25 ergy has suffered, and will continue to suffer irreparable injury including, without limitation, a

26 loss of market share and business opportunities arising from Prime Secured’s failure to promote

27 the Products.

28 ///


                                                    -7-                                       COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671         Document 1     Filed 12/03/24       Page 8 of 12


 1                                    SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION

 2                                         (Breach of Contract)

 3                          Failure to Fulfill Minimum Volume Requirement

 4           61.   Plaintiff realleges and incorporates by reference the allegations set forth in Para-

 5 graphs 1-60 by reference as if more fully set forth herein.

 6           62.   Pursuant to the Agreement, the Initial Term was for a period of three (3) years.

 7           63.   Pursuant to Section 7.1, the Agreement absent written notice of termination issued

 8 at least sixty (60) days prior to the expiration of the Initial Term, the Agreement automatically re-

 9 newed for an additional one-year period (the “Renewal Term”).

10           64.   Prime Secured did not issue a written notice of termination at least sixty (60) days

11 prior the expiration of the Initial Term.

12           65.   Prime Secured did not terminate the Agreement at least sixty (60) days prior to the

13 expiration of the Initial Term.

14           66.   The Agreement renewed and extended for an additional one (1) year commencing

15 on June 30, 2024 and ending on June 30, 2025. See Ex. A.

16           67.   The Agreement between Prime Secured and Quanergy provides that during the Re-

17 newal Term, Prime Secured is required to purchase at least 100 units of the Products during the

18 Renewal Term.

19           68.   To date, during the Renewal Term, Prime Secured has refused to discuss the pur-

20 chase of additional Products.

21           69.   Additionally, by acts and omissions set forth above, Prime Secured clearly and une-

22 quivocally repudiated its obligations under the Agreement and Purchase Order.

23           70.   Prime Secured expressly and/or via repudiation, breached the Agreement by failing

24 and/or refusing to purchase Products during the Renewal Term.

25           71.   Pursuant to Section 3.6 of the Agreement, Prime Secured is liable for interest on

26 any delinquent amounts owed to Quanergy at the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month or (b) the maximum

27 rate permitted under California law.

28           72.   Section 3.6 of the Agreement provides that Prime Secured shall be responsible for


                                                    -8-                                        COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
           Case 5:24-cv-08671        Document 1      Filed 12/03/24      Page 9 of 12


 1 reasonable attorneys’ fees and other costs incurred by Quanergy in connection with litigation to

 2 enforce the Agreement if Quanergy prevails.

 3           73.   As a direct and proximate result of the material breach of the Agreement by Prime

 4 Secured, Quanergy has sustained general, special and incidental damages in an amount not less

 5 than $75,000 plus interest at the lesser of (a) 1.5% per month or (b) the maximum rate permitted

 6 under California law, and Quanergy’s reasonable attorneys’ fees and costs.

 7           74.   Furthermore, as a direct and proximate result of Prime Secured’s breaches, Quan-

 8 ergy has suffered, and will continue to suffer irreparable injury including, without limitation, a

 9 loss of market share and business opportunities arising from Prime Secured’s failure to promote

10 the Products.

11                                    THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION

12                                         (Unjust Enrichment)

13           75.   Quanergy re-alleges and incorporates by reference the allegations set forth in para-

14 graphs 1 through 74 above and incorporates each allegation herein by reference.

15           76.   In the alternative to its claims for breach of contract, Quanergy asserts that Prime

16 Secured derived a benefit from conduct that is unlawful, inequitable and fundamentally unjust to

17 Quanergy’s great harm and detriment.

18           77.   Specifically, and without limitation, Prime Secured (i) gained valuable information

19 regarding the features and capabilities of the Products and the differences between the Products

20 and competing goods; and (ii) falsely led Quanergy to believe that Prime Secured would continue

21 to market and promote Quanergy’s products.

22           78.   Prime Secured’s conduct was unlawful, inequitable, and fundamental unjust.

23           79.   Prime Secured’s derived a direct and/or indirect economic benefit from its unlawful

24 and inequitable conduct including, without limitation, increased market share within the Territory.

25           80.   The retention of said benefit by Prime Secured is unjust and contrary to equitable

26 principles.

27           81.   As set forth above, Quanergy has suffered and continues to suffer harm for which

28 legal remedies are inadequate.


                                                    -9-                                        COMPLAINT

     164514885.6
          Case 5:24-cv-08671       Document 1        Filed 12/03/24      Page 10 of 12


 1           82.   Equity requires that Prime Secured account for all benefits (including profits) de-

 2 rived from its unlawful and unjust enrichment.

 3           83.   Equity requires that Prime Secured disgorge all benefit (including profits) derived

 4 from its unlawful and unjust enrichment.

 5                                       PRAYER FOR RELIEF

 6           WHEREFORE, Quanergy prays for relief and judgment against each Defendant as fol-

 7 lows:

 8           A.    For damages in an amount to be proven, but not less than $75,000;

 9           B.    Specific performance or one or more provisions in the Agreement;

10           C.    Injunctive relief in the form of a decree enjoining, inter alia, ongoing violations of

11 the Agreement for which monetary damages are inadequate;

12           D.    Judgment in favor of Quanergy and against Prime Secured in an amount to be de-

13 termined at trial, including, but not limited to, general damages, direct damages, consequential

14 damages, compensatory damages and pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, as permitted by

15 law;

16           E.    An award of Quanergy’s reasonable attorneys’ fees, costs, and expenses pursuant to

17 the Agreement and applicable law; and

18           F.    Such other and further relief as the Court deems just, equitable and proper.

19

20           Dated: December 3, 2024.             Respectfully submitted,
